installation.note: top is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: top displays real-time information about running processes, CPU usage, memory usage, and system load. It's an interactive process monitor - you can sort, filter, and kill processes. While htop is more user-friendly, top is available everywhere and is the standard process monitor.

syntax.description: Display real-time process information. Interactive - use keyboard commands to sort, filter, and manage processes. Press 'q' to quit.

options.description: Show only processes for specified user

output_explanation.notes: Shows real-time system and process information. Updates continuously. Press 'q' to quit, 'k' to kill process, arrow keys to navigate.

examples.use_case: Monitor system performance and running processes

examples.title: Non-interactive (one snapshot)
examples.description: Get one snapshot of processes (for scripts)
examples.output: (single snapshot of process list, then exits)

output_explanation.notes: Outputs one snapshot then exits. Perfect for scripts. No interactive mode.

misconceptions.title: top and htop are the same
misconceptions.reality: htop is more user-friendly with better UI, colors, and mouse support. top is more basic but available everywhere. htop requires installation, top is built-in.
misconceptions.tip: htop = better UI, requires installation. top = basic, available everywhere. Both do similar things.

common_pitfalls.solution: Press 'q' to quit top. Other keys: 'k' to kill process, arrow keys to navigate, 'h' for help.

related_commands.relationship: Process monitor; htop is improved version of top
related_commands.description: Interactive process monitor (more user-friendly than top)

related_commands.relationship: Process list; ps shows snapshot, top shows real-time
related_commands.description: Show process snapshot (top shows real-time updates)

best_practices: Press 'k' then enter PID to kill process
Press 'h' for help to see all commands
Use arrow keys to navigate and sort
Check load average - should be < number of CPU cores
performance_tips: Updates every few seconds by default
Use htop for better performance on large systems

additional_notes.interactive: top is interactive - use keyboard commands. Press 'q' to quit, 'h' for help.
additional_notes.vs_htop: top = basic, available everywhere. htop = better UI, requires installation. Both monitor processes.
additional_notes.common_usage: Very common: top (monitor), top -u user (filter by user), top -b -n 1 (script output)
